the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
library: a place or collection where books or other resources can be borrowed
He spends every Saturday morning at the local library.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
lends: gives something temporarily, expecting it back (he/she/it)
The library lends tools as well as books to local residents.
tools: plural of tool; devices used to carry out tasks
It has no words for the small things like kitchen tools or playground arguments.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
drills: The workshop has several drills of different sizes.
spend: to use time or money on something
They spend every summer visiting their grandparents in the countryside.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
entire: She spent the entire afternoon cleaning out the garage.
working: Understanding the pattern is the first step towards working around it.
life: the state of being alive, or the period from birth to death
She moved to the countryside to enjoy a quieter life.
switched: turned something off or on, or changed to something else
He switched the lights off before leaving the office for the night.
off: not connected, operating, or switched on
Please turn the lights off before you leave the room.
few: a small number of; not many
Only a few students finished the exam before the bell rang.
towns: plural of town; populated areas smaller than cities
A few towns decided that was a problem worth fixing.
decided: made a choice or judgment after considering options
She decided to move to the countryside after years in the city.
was: past tense of 'be', used for the first/third person singular
Half an hour after a lesson ends, much of what was said is already gone.
problem: a matter that is difficult to deal with or solve
The main problem with the plan was its enormous cost.
worth: having a value or deserving of something
Unless something marks it as worth keeping, it is allowed to fade.
fixing: the act of repairing or solving something
Fixing the old bridge took the whole summer.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
electric: They bought an electric kettle that boils water in seconds.
drill: a tool used for making holes
He used an electric drill to hang the new shelves.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
least: Of all the options, this one costs the least money.
used: past tense of use; employed something for a purpose
A language kept only in books can be studied but not used.
objects: physical things that can be seen or touched
The museum displays ancient objects found during the excavation.
households: houses and their occupants regarded as units, plural
Many households now rely on solar panels for electricity.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
estimates: approximate calculations or judgements of a value
Estimates of its lifetime working time vary considerably.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
lifetime: the length of time a person or thing lives or lasts
The bridge was designed to last well beyond a human lifetime.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
vary: to be different or change according to circumstances
Opinions on the new policy vary widely among residents.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
everyone: Everyone who has measured it agrees on the shape of the answer.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
measured: found the size, amount, or degree of something
Researchers measured the temperature of the water every hour.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
agrees: has the same opinion, or consents to something
Nearly everyone agrees that the old bridge needs urgent repair.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
shape: the outward form or outline of something
The cookie cutter gave the biscuits a star shape.
answer: a response given to a question or problem
Her answer to the interview question impressed every member of the panel.
handful: a small quantity or number of something
Only a handful of students turned up for the early lecture.
minutes: units of time equal to sixty seconds
The bus arrived only a few minutes late.
year: Everyone agrees the device runs for only a handful of minutes a year.
spread: to extend over a larger area or reach more people over time
The fire spread quickly through the dry forest.
across: from one side of something to the other
A narrow bridge stretches across the river near the old mill.
decade: The city's population has doubled over the past decade.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
rest: the part of something that remains, or a period of relaxation
phần còn lại, sự nghỉ ngơi
After a short rest, they continued walking up the hill.
sits: is located in a particular place
The old castle sits on a hill overlooking the valley.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
cupboard: a piece of furniture with doors and shelves, used for storage
The plates and bowls are kept in the kitchen cupboard.
observation: the act of watching something carefully, or a comment based on this
Her observation about the traffic pattern proved to be correct.
old: having lived or existed for a long time; not new or young
The old bridge was replaced after decades of heavy use.
response: a reaction or reply to something
The government's response to the flood was criticized as slow.
fairly: The instructions were fairly easy to follow.
recent: happening or made a short time ago
Her most recent film received excellent reviews from critics.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
past: gone by in time; belonging to an earlier time
Over the past year, the company has doubled its workforce.
decades: The old bridge has stood for decades without major repairs.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
countries: nations, each with its own government and territory
Trade agreements now link dozens of countries across three continents.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
opened: made something no longer closed; started operating for the first time
The new library opened to the public last spring.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
usually: A machine that appears to be held up by one principle is usually held up by several.
called: named or referred to by a particular term
The recipe uses a fermented paste called miso for extra flavour.
tool: a device or implement used to carry out a particular task
Towns have opened tool libraries with ladders, sanders and tile cutters.
libraries: places or collections where books or other resources can be borrowed
Public libraries offer free internet access to local residents.
rooms: spaces within a building enclosed by walls
The old hostel has ten simple rooms for travelers.
ladders: structures of steps used for climbing up or down
Workers used tall ladders to reach the damaged roof tiles.
sanders: tools or machines used to smooth surfaces by rubbing
The workshop lends out sanders and other power tools.
tile: a thin, flat piece of material used to cover roofs, walls or floors
Towns have opened tool libraries with ladders, sanders, tile cutters and pressure washers.
cutters: tools or machines used for cutting
The workshop lends out saws, drills, and tile cutters free of charge.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
washers: machines for washing; also small flat rings used with bolts
The tool library lends out ladders, sanders and pressure washers.
lent: gave something temporarily, expecting it back (past of lend)
đã được cho mượn, đã cho vay
The neighbour lent us a ladder to fix the roof.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
much: to a great extent or degree
The new design does not cost much more than the old one.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
terms: words with specific meanings, or conditions of an agreement
The contract lists the terms both parties must agree to follow.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
books: written or printed works with pages bound together
The old library holds thousands of rare books from past centuries.
economics: the study of how goods and money are produced and used
She studied economics at university before joining the bank.
straightforward: easy to understand or do; uncomplicated
Filling in the online form is fairly straightforward.
costs: requires the payment of a specified amount of money
A round trip by taxi costs more than the entire bus fare for a week.
hundred: He paid a hundred dollars for the used bicycle.
pounds: The jacket costs about eighty pounds in that shop.
twice: In a cold kitchen the dough may need twice that time to rise.
expensive: The engine burns more fuel, and on a long voyage that becomes expensive.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
money: coins and banknotes used to pay for goods and services
They saved money for years before buying their first house.
space: an empty or open area, or the region beyond Earth's atmosphere
There isn't enough space in the room for another desk.
occupies: fills or takes up a space, time, or position
The old library still occupies the corner of the square.
shared: divided among several people, or held in common
The siblings shared a bedroom for most of their childhood.
between: in the space or time separating two things
The old road runs between two small villages in the valley.
forty: The bus was carrying about forty passengers.
each: every one of two or more things, considered separately
Each student received a copy of the new textbook.
them: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the object
I called them yesterday but nobody answered the phone.
very: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger
The soup tasted very good after such a cold walk.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
takes: gets hold of, requires, or needs an amount of time or effort
The journey usually takes about two hours by train.
up: towards a higher place or position
Neighbourhoods with few trees and little open space heat up fastest.
none: not any of a group of people or things
None of the students had heard of the composer before.
room: a space within a building enclosed by walls
She rearranged the furniture to make the room feel larger.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
difficulties: problems that make something hard to do
The company faced serious financial difficulties last year.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
financial: The company faced serious financial problems last year.
break: to separate into pieces, or stop working, suddenly
Cheap umbrellas often break after just one windy day.
unlike: Tools break, and unlike a damaged book a damaged tool can be dangerous.
damaged: harmed or injured in a way that reduces value or usefulness
The damaged bridge remained closed to traffic for several months.
book: a written or printed work with pages bound together
She borrowed a book about ancient history from the library.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
dangerous: likely to cause harm, injury, or loss
Riding without a helmet can be extremely dangerous.
somebody: Somebody left their umbrella in the meeting room.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
check: to examine something to make sure it is correct or safe
Always check the label before giving medicine to a child.
item: a single article, object, or entry in a list
Please check each item carefully before you sign the receipt.
return: the act of coming or going back
sự trở lại, sự trả lại
On his return, he found the house exactly as he left it.
sharpen: to make an edge or point finer or more cutting
He stopped to sharpen the kitchen knife before slicing the onions.
needs: The garden needs watering twice a week during summer.
sharpening: making an edge or point finer or more cutting
Sharpening the blade only takes a couple of minutes.
decide: make a choice or judgment after considering options
The committee will decide next week whether to approve the funding.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
machine: a device with moving parts that performs a task
The factory installed a new machine to speed up packaging.
reached: arrived at or got as far as a place or level
The negotiators finally reached an agreement after weeks of talks.
end: the final part or point of something
Save the best joke for the end of your speech.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
invisible: Radio waves are invisible but carry signals across long distances.
members: people who belong to a group or organisation
The committee has twelve members who meet monthly.
consumes: uses up a resource, or eats or drinks something
The old factory still consumes far more electricity than newer ones.
staff: the group of people who work for an organisation
The hotel staff were extremely helpful during our stay.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists
There is a small cafe just around the corner.
second: coming after the first in order
The second attempt succeeded where the first had failed.
quieter: making less noise; calmer than something else
The countryside felt much quieter than the noisy city centre.
difficulty: the state of being hard to do or understand
She had no difficulty finishing the race in record time.
borrowing: the act of taking and using something that belongs to someone else, promising to return it
Borrowing tools from the neighbours saved them a lot of money.
requires: needs something, or demands it officially
This recipe requires fresh herbs and a hot oven.
planning: the process of making detailed plans for something
Careful planning made the wedding day run smoothly.
you: used to refer to the person being spoken to
The method also feels worse while you are doing it.
must: used to show that something is necessary or certain
You must show identification before entering the building.
know: to have information or understanding about something
Do you know the fastest way to get to the airport?
advance: beforehand; before something is due to happen
Tickets must be booked in advance for the weekend show.
job: a paid position of regular employment or a task to do
She found a part-time job at the local bakery.
someone: Someone called while you were out this afternoon.
else: in addition to, or other than, someone or something already mentioned
Ask someone else if you need a second opinion on this.
booked: They booked the hotel room three months before their trip.
owning: having something as one's own property
Owning a car in the city can be more trouble than it's worth.
nothing: There was nothing left in the fridge by Friday evening.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
people: human beings in general, considered as a group of individuals
Many people prefer walking to work during the warm summer months.
convenience: the quality of being easy or useful to do or use
Online banking offers the convenience of paying bills from home.
outweighs: is greater in importance, value, or influence than something else
For many travellers, the convenience of flying outweighs the expense.
cost: the amount of money needed to buy, do, or produce something
The cost of the renovation was far higher than the family expected.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
amount: a quantity of something, especially an unspecified one
A small amount of sugar can bring out the flavour of tomatoes.
arithmetic: the branch of mathematics dealing with basic calculations
The young student practised arithmetic every evening before dinner.
changes: plural of change; alterations or differences from before
The new law brought major changes to how taxes are collected.
mind: a person's thoughts, opinions, or way of thinking
After weeks of doubt, she finally made up her mind to move abroad.
where: It changes where the effort goes, away from the comfortable hours of reading.
these: used to refer to people or things nearby or just mentioned
These shoes are far more comfortable than my old ones.
lasted: continued for a period of time
đã tồn tại được, kéo dài
The meeting lasted almost three hours longer than planned.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
done: Have you done your homework for tomorrow yet?
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
becoming: The town is becoming a popular spot for young families.
something: She said something that made everyone in the room laugh.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
store: a supply of something kept for future use, or a shop
The farm kept a small store of grain for the winter.
shown: past participle of show: made clear or demonstrated
New members are shown around the building on their first day.
how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
use: to employ something for a particular purpose
What cannot be coined is a reason to use them.
borrow: to take and use something that belongs to someone else, promising to return it
He asked his neighbour if he could borrow a ladder for the weekend.
repairs: work done to fix something damaged
The repairs to the bridge cost more than expected.
demonstrated: shown clearly through action or example
The teacher demonstrated the experiment before letting students try it.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
performed: carried out or executed an action or task
The ceremony was performed exactly as tradition required, without any changes.
building: a structure with walls and a roof, such as a house or office
The old building was renovated into modern apartments last year.
turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
place: a particular position, location, or area
This quiet park is my favorite place to read on weekends.
learn: to gain knowledge or skill through study or experience
Children often learn new languages faster than adults.
skill: the ability to do something well, gained through training or practice
Cooking well takes years of practice and skill to master.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
otherwise: in a different way, or under different circumstances; if not
Wear a helmet; otherwise, you risk a serious head injury.
paid: gave money in exchange for goods or services (past tense)
They paid extra for faster delivery of the package.
supply: to provide something that is needed
The factory supplies parts to car makers across the region.
catalogue: a complete list of items, often with descriptions
The library keeps an online catalogue of all its books.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
outsiders: people who do not belong to a particular group; plural of outsider
The close-knit village was often wary of outsiders.
underestimate: to judge something as smaller, less important, or less capable than it really is
The catalogue is the part outsiders underestimate.
easy: The test was easy enough that most students finished early.
lend: to give something to someone temporarily, expecting it back
Could you lend me your umbrella for the afternoon?
knowing: having information or understanding about something
Knowing when to stop working is an important skill for bakers.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
nine: She has worked at the bakery for nine years now.
suits: is convenient or right for someone or something
This job suits people who enjoy working with their hands.
wall: an upright structure that encloses or divides a space
Tall buildings bounce heat from wall to wall instead of letting it escape.
soft: not hard or firm to the touch
The kitten's fur felt incredibly soft against her hand.
brick: a rectangular block used for building walls
The old house was built entirely of red brick.
knowledge: information, understanding, or skill gained through experience
Her knowledge of local plants proved useful during the hike.
sit: to rest with the body supported on the buttocks
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable while you wait.
somewhere: in, at, or to an unspecified or unknown place
They plan to travel somewhere warm this winter.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
kind: a type or category of something
This kind of bread takes several hours to rise properly.
employing: giving someone paid work, or making use of something
Most libraries end up employing at least one person for advice.
person: a human being regarded as an individual
Every person in the room agreed that the plan needed changes.
whose: belonging to or associated with which person
Most librarians end up being the person whose real job is giving advice.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
advice: guidance or recommendations offered about future action
Her grandmother's advice on saving money still guides her today.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
lending: the act of giving something temporarily, expecting it back
The bank tightened its lending rules after the crisis.
desk: a table used for writing or working, or a service counter
She left the documents on the front desk for you.
excuse: a reason given to justify or explain an action
cái cớ, lý do biện minh
The lending desk works as an excuse for the real conversation.
conversation: a talk between two or more people
They had a long conversation about their plans for the future.
shift: to move or change gradually from one state to another
Public opinion began to shift after the documentary aired.
explains: makes something clear by describing it in detail
This explains why rereading notes feels productive but works so poorly.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
idea: a thought or plan about what to do
She had a brilliant idea for the school fundraiser.
spreads: extends over a larger area or reaches more people over time
News spreads quickly on social media these days.
unevenly: in a way that is not equal or consistent
That shift explains why the idea spreads unevenly.
way: As a way of saving money, it is easy to copy and abandon.
saving: the act of keeping money or resources rather than spending them
Saving a little each month adds up over the years.
copy: make or produce something identical to or imitating an original
Students should not copy answers directly from a classmate's homework.
abandon: to stop doing or using something completely
They had to abandon the project halfway through due to lack of funds.
neighbourhood: a district or area within a town or city
khu phố, cộng đồng dân cư
The bakery has served this quiet neighbourhood for forty years.
keeps: continues to have, hold, or maintain something (he/she/it)
Regular exercise keeps the body strong and flexible.
practical: concerned with actual application rather than theory
She gave us some practical tips for managing our time better.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
build: to construct something by putting parts together
They plan to build a new library in the town centre.
replaced: had something new put in its place
The old traffic lights were replaced with a modern system.
anything: If you need anything during the trip, just call me.
arrives: reaches a place or comes to happen
Spring arrives a little earlier each year in this region.
delivery: the act of bringing goods to a destination
We are still waiting for the delivery of our new sofa.
van: a medium-sized vehicle for carrying goods or people
The bakery delivers fresh bread in a small van every morning.
